findingRechecks.evidence: Regenerated desktop screenshots put maximum above zero on the vertical value axis. Narrow screenshots put zero at the left and maximum at the right of the horizontal value axis. Browser checks confirm this ordering in both periods, themes and text sizes.
All four narrow screenshots keep weekday abbreviations intact. Browser checks confirm no category-label overflow for weekday and Week 1–4 labels at 375px and 1280px with 100% and 200% root text size.

verification.matrix: 375px and 1280px × light and dark × 100% and 200% root text × week to month to week.
verification.barProportions: Every selected and previous bar matches its source value divided by the shared ceiling, within 0.1 CSS px of the available plot length. Horizontal widths and vertical heights both checked.
verification.periodSwitching: Seven daily buckets switch to four weekly buckets and back. Totals, comparison totals, percent change, summaries, scale and table rows remain consistent with the unchanged data. Week: 1,120 vs 970, +15.5%, scale 300. Month: 3,794 vs 3,288, +15.4%, scale 1,200.
verification.layout: No document overflow or category-label overflow in any browser case. Regenerated screenshots show readable axes, intact categories and distinguishable solid/striped bars in both themes, including narrow enlarged text.
verification.runnerChecks: Six supplied reports contain no errors, failed requests, overflow, contrast failures, unlabeled controls or small targets.
verification.guidance: Read the new shared charts reference. Its final paragraph explicitly addresses intact short labels, alternative horizontal layout and zero/maximum placement at matching axis ends.
verification.limits: Supplied screenshots cover the default seven-day view. Other period and desktop enlarged-text checks used browser geometry and DOM inspection.
